description: Run AI Output page — displays the full AI conversation transcript from a workflow run. Users can select between multiple AI sessions (setup, agentic, completion), read the complete conversation, view session statistics, manage auto-continue settings, and control live execution.

groups.name: AI Session Selection and Navigation
groups.description: A single workflow run may produce multiple AI sessions — setup sessions, agentic iterations, and completion sessions. Users need to navigate between these sessions to read the specific conversation they are interested in. The session selector provides a dropdown listing all available sessions with metadata (type, status, duration, message count), plus an 'All Sessions' option that concatenates all output chronologically. This navigation is essential for understanding the full AI interaction across a multi-phase workflow.

assertions.description: The user can select between different AI sessions using a dropdown or selector, with each session labeled by its type (setup, agentic, completion) and number, enabling navigation through the multi-session conversation history

The user can see quick statistics for each session including duration, message count, and session type, helping them understand the scope and nature of each AI interaction without reading the full transcript
The user can select an 'All Sessions' view that combines output from all AI sessions in chronological order, providing a complete end-to-end transcript of all AI activity during the run

groups.name: Conversation Transcript Reading
groups.description: The primary purpose of this page is reading the AI conversation. The transcript shows the full exchange between the user's prompt, the AI's reasoning, the commands AI issued, and their results. The conversation is rendered with proper formatting (markdown, code blocks) and fills the main content area for maximum readability. Users come here to understand exactly what the AI did, why it made certain decisions, and what it learned during the workflow execution.

assertions.description: The user can read the full AI conversation transcript for the selected session, rendered with proper formatting including markdown, code blocks, and command output, in a scrollable area that maximizes readability
The user can copy the AI conversation output to the clipboard for use in bug reports, documentation, or sharing with team members, without having to manually select and copy text

When the AI session includes iterative loops (verification-fix cycles), the user can see the loop structure in the output, distinguishing between different iterations and understanding how the AI progressed through the problem

groups.name: Execution Controls and Status
groups.description: The AI Output page is not just a passive viewer — it also provides execution controls for managing AI sessions. Users can see the current execution status (running, complete, failed, stopped), control auto-continue behavior, stop running sessions, restart completed ones, and manage session deletion. The status banner at the top communicates the live execution state, and controls allow real-time intervention during active runs.

assertions.description: The user can see a status banner showing the current state of the AI session (running, complete, failed, stopped), providing immediate context about whether the conversation is still active or has concluded
The user can toggle auto-continue behavior, which controls whether the system automatically starts new AI sessions when the current one completes, enabling hands-off iterative execution
When a session is running, the user can stop it, providing emergency control when the AI is taking an undesirable path or consuming too many resources

groups.name: Empty and Loading States
groups.description: The AI Output page must handle various data availability states. When no run is selected, it prompts the user to select one. When a run has no AI output (pure automation workflows), it shows an appropriate empty state. During live execution, the output streams in progressively. The page must also handle the case where AI session data is still being written to the database (output chunks arrive asynchronously).

assertions.description: When no run is selected, the user sees a clear message prompting them to select a run, with helpful context about how to get started with AI output viewing
When the selected run has no AI sessions (pure automation workflow), the user sees an informative empty state explaining that no AI output is available for this run type
During active execution, the AI output streams in progressively, allowing the user to watch the conversation unfold in real time rather than waiting for the session to complete
